question.text: A physical quantity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> is given as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><msqrt><mi>d</mi></msqrt></mrow></mfrac></math>. The percentage error in the measurement of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>c</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi></math> are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>%</mo><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>2</mn><mo>%</mo><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>3</mn><mo>%</mo></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>%</mo></math> respectively. The percentage error in the measurement of quantity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> will be

solution.text:
The given quantity is P=a2b3cd.

The percentage error for a quantity can be given by the formula ∆xx×100.

Relation of the relative errors will be,

ΔPP=2Δaa+3Δbb+Δcc+12Δdd

Hence, the percentage error is calculated by substituting the values,

ΔPP×100=2×1+3×2+3+12×4=13%.
